messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Use and access.** “The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel named in writing and approved by the design owner before access. Each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The same requirements apply to external personnel and replacements. The testing house is responsible for their compliance. Neither the testing house nor anyone receiving the material may use it to develop a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The testing house may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the tests, with encryption at rest and in transit. It may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. Fixture files and physical fixtures must be kept secure and used only for these tests. The test report may retain measurements and results, but must exclude CAD geometry unless the design owner approves its inclusion in writing.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the testing house must destroy its copies of the drawings, CAD geometry, derivative fixture files and physical fixtures, and obtain confirmation of destruction from any approved external personnel. Within the same period, it must provide a signed certificate identifying the materials destroyed and the date and method of destruction. If the design owner identifies a specific, reasonable concern about completeness, the testing house must obtain independent certification addressing that concern. Verification under this clause does not require design-owner access to the site.”

Can your backup system meet the 30-day deadline, and can your laboratory retain its required test record using measurements, fixture identifiers and setup descriptions alone? If either point needs an exception, please specify the material and minimum retention period so we can agree on narrow wording.

**Direct answers first.**

**Backups: 30 days is not achievable as drafted.** Our encrypted backup set is immutable and rolls off on a fixed cycle; we cannot selectively purge a single file from a sealed snapshot without breaking the integrity of the whole set. We can meet 30 days for all live, working and archive stores, and for the machining shop and lab. For backup media we need a run-off exception with a hard outside date of 90 days, no restore other than disaster recovery, and continuing confidentiality throughout. That is a real exception, not a drafting preference — please price it as one.

**Lab record: yes, with one narrow addition.** Our accredited lab can retain a conforming technical record built from measurements, results, fixture identifiers, setup descriptions, equipment IDs and calibration certificates — no CAD geometry, no dimensioned views, no fixture drawings. The one item we cannot drop is traceability metadata: drawing number, revision index and date, so an assessor can tie a result to the configuration tested. That is identification, not geometry. Minimum retention we are required to hold is **two years** for calibration and associated technical records; we propose that as the ceiling too, so nothing lives longer than the obligation requires.

**Replacement wording — Destruction and verification.**

> "Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test work, the testing house must destroy all live and archived copies of the drawings, CAD geometry and derivative fixture files, destroy or render unusable the physical fixtures derived from that geometry, and obtain written confirmation of destruction from each approved external recipient. Acceptance is deemed to occur 15 business days after delivery of the final report unless the design owner gives written notice of specific non-conformities.
>
> Two exceptions apply. (a) **Backup run-off:** copies residing in immutable or routine backup media need not be destroyed within 30 days, provided they are deleted or overwritten in the ordinary cycle no later than 90 days after the destruction date, are not accessed or restored other than for disaster recovery, and remain subject to this agreement until deleted. If restored, they must be re-destroyed within 10 days. (b) **Retained record:** the testing house and its accredited laboratory may retain, for two years and no longer, the test record consisting of measurements, results, fixture identifiers, textual setup descriptions, equipment identifiers, calibration certificates, and drawing number, revision index and date. The retained record must contain no CAD geometry, no dimensioned drawings and no fixture design files. It remains subject to the use and confidentiality restrictions and may be used only for accreditation, calibration traceability, and defence of legal claims.
>
> Within the 30-day period the testing house must provide a signed certificate identifying the categories of material destroyed, the date and method of destruction, the confirmations received from external recipients, and the scope of material held under exceptions (a) and (b). If the design owner identifies a specific, reasonable concern about completeness, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality will address that concern, at the design owner's cost unless the audit reveals material non-compliance, in which case the testing house bears it. Verification under this clause gives no right of access to any site."

**Two things we still need to resolve, and they are the reason the current draft does not work for us.**

**1. Named-person pre-approval will stop the job.** We use a specialist machining shop for fixtures and an accredited laboratory for the vibration runs. Naming every individual and waiting for approval before access is unworkable when a shift changes or a specialist falls ill mid-programme. We propose an approved-recipient annex plus notice-based substitution:

> "Access is limited to personnel of the testing house and of the organisations listed in Annex A (Approved Recipients), each bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house must maintain a current access roster and provide it on request. Personnel may be added or substituted by written notice identifying the individual, the recipient organisation and the scope of access. Substitution takes effect on notice unless the design owner objects within three business days on reasonable grounds relating to confidentiality or competitive conflict. The testing house remains responsible for compliance. Adding an organisation not in Annex A requires prior written approval, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed."

We will name the machining shop and the laboratory in Annex A now and accept that new *organisations* need your consent. What we cannot accept is a veto over individual substitutions inside organisations you have already cleared. If three business days is too fast for your conflict check, we can pre-clear a bench of named alternates at kickoff so substitution is same-day against a list you already approved — tell me which you prefer.

**2. Verification cannot mean site access.** Our test work runs at a shared customer facility. We cannot grant unannounced inspections there, and we cannot grant geometry-adjacent walkthroughs of another customer's area at all. The clause above closes with "no right of access to any site" and routes verification through the certificate and, on specific concern, an independent auditor. If you need more than that, the tradeable options are: a scheduled remote evidence session showing redacted deletion logs and the destruction confirmations; or an records-only review by the auditor of our document register, with no geometry shown. We will fund the certificate and cooperate fully with a scoped audit. We will not open a third party's site.

**Smaller edits to your other two clauses.**

- *Working copies*: add "including copies reasonably necessary for an Approved Recipient to design and fabricate fixtures and to perform the tests." As drafted, "the testing house may make the working copies" does not clearly authorise the machining shop to hold a file at all.
- *Fixtures*: destruction should reach fixtures "derived from that geometry." Generic clamps, shims and adapters that embody none of your geometry are our tooling and stay ours. Happy to certify that no design-derived feature survives in anything we keep.
- *Non-compete*: we accept the restriction. Please add "Nothing in this clause restricts the use of general skills, experience or fixture-design methods that do not embody the design owner's geometry or confidential information." Otherwise a fixture house that has learned how to clamp actuators is arguably barred from ordinary work.
- *Report*: excluding geometry is fine. We need the report to carry drawing number and revision so the result is traceable; that is consistent with the retained-record carve-out.

**Questions back to you.** Is 90 days acceptable for backup run-off, or do you need a shorter outside date with a different mechanism? Does the two-year retained record with revision metadata satisfy your traceability concern, or is there a specific artefact you believe you need that we have not listed? And on verification — what would an independent certificate need to say for you to consider the matter closed without a site visit? If you tell me the evidence you actually want, we can probably produce it in a form that does not touch the customer facility.

We accept the pre-cleared bench, a 90-day backup run-off and the two-year technical record. Drawing number, revision index and date give us the traceability we need. We need no additional artefact. A signed independent certificate can close a specific destruction concern without a site visit. We propose the following wording to settle the remaining points.

**Named personnel.** “Before first access, the parties will agree Annex A in writing. It will name the machining shop, the accredited laboratory and each authorised individual, including alternates, with their organisation, role and permitted access. A named alternate may take over immediately within that scope. The testing house must record the change, notify the design owner that day and promptly revoke access when an individual ceases to need it. A new individual, organisation or expansion of access requires prior written approval, which the design owner will not unreasonably withhold or delay. Every authorised individual and external organisation must be bound by written confidentiality and use terms at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house remains responsible for their compliance.”

**Copies, fixtures and reuse.** “Named personnel may make encrypted working copies within their approved scope solely for the agreed vibration tests. The machining shop may receive the minimum geometry needed to fabricate the fixtures, and the laboratory may receive the material needed to set up, perform and report the tests. The testing house must ensure that destruction of a design-derived fixture removes or destroys every feature embodying the design owner’s geometry. It may retain generic tooling and certify that no design-derived feature survives in the tooling retained. No recipient may use the design owner’s drawings, geometry or other confidential information to develop a competing product. Recipients may use general skills, experience and fixture-design methods that do not embody that geometry or confidential information.”

**Acceptance and backup dates.** We accept deemed acceptance after 15 business days. A timely written notice identifying specific non-conformities suspends deemed acceptance until a corrected final report is delivered, when a fresh 15-business-day review period begins. For the destruction clause, we propose this common starting point so the 30- and 90-day periods run together.

> “The trigger date is the date of written or deemed acceptance of the final report, or the date of earlier termination. The 30-day destruction and certification deadline runs from the trigger date. Only encrypted copies already held in sealed backup sets that cannot be selectively purged qualify for run-off. Those copies must expire within 90 calendar days of the trigger date and remain subject to the confidentiality and use restrictions throughout. Access and restoration are permitted solely for disaster recovery. Any restored copy must be isolated from project use and deleted within 10 days of restoration and in all cases by day 90. Within five business days after final expiry, the testing house must certify the date on which the last qualifying backup expired.”

**Technical record.** We accept your listed contents, permitted purposes and geometry exclusions. Drawing number, revision index and date may also appear in the final report. We propose measuring the two years from final report delivery, or from termination if no final report was delivered. At expiry, the testing house and laboratory must delete the retained record and the testing house must confirm deletion in writing within five business days.

**Verification.** We accept your 30-day certificate and audit cost allocation. For a specific, reasonable concern, a confidential, records-only review is sufficient. We propose this closing language.

> “The independent auditor’s signed certificate must identify the concern reviewed, the recipients and material categories covered, and the evidence examined, which may include redacted deletion logs, backup expiry records and external destruction confirmations. It must state whether the evidence verifies compliance with the applicable deadline, identify any permitted holdings and their expiry dates, and describe any discrepancy or gap in the evidence. The concern is closed when the auditor verifies compliance or certifies completion of any necessary corrective action. Verification confers no right of site access and requires no disclosure of CAD geometry or another customer’s information.”

**Where we agree outright:** the fixture-destruction standard and generic-tooling certification; the reuse and general-skills language; drawing number, revision index and date in the final report; two years measured from final report delivery or termination; the auditor's certificate contents and closure mechanic; no site access, no geometry, no other customer's information. Those are settled.

Four points need wording before we can sign, plus one practical allowance we should trade for something you want.

**1. Backup eligibility has a gap that will bite us both.** Your run-off covers copies "already held in sealed backup sets" at the trigger date. But we will still be working during the 30-day window — closing out the report file, archiving, answering your review — and the ordinary nightly cycle will seal fresh sets containing that material. Those sets are not "already held" at the trigger date, so as drafted they fall outside run-off and we would be in breach on day 31 for something we cannot purge. Fix:

> "Only encrypted copies held in sealed backup sets that cannot be selectively purged qualify for run-off, whether held at the trigger date or created in the ordinary backup cycle before the 30-day destruction deadline. After the live destruction date, no further backup of the material will be made. Restored copies will be isolated from project use, excluded from backup, and deleted within 10 days of restoration and in all cases by day 90."

We will certify the last-expiry date within five business days of final expiry, and earlier if the last set rolls off sooner. We accept day 90 as a hard outside date, not a target.

**2. The acceptance loop needs a long-stop.** A suspension that restarts a fresh 15-business-day clock on each corrected report can, in principle, run indefinitely — and while it runs we are holding your geometry, which is the exposure you are trying to minimise. We are content that a notice must identify specific non-conformities; we ask that they be measured against the agreed test specification, and that a dispute cannot keep the material alive:

> "A timely written notice must identify specific non-conformities against the agreed test specification and suspends deemed acceptance until a corrected final report is delivered, when a fresh 15-business-day review period begins. If acceptance has not occurred within 60 calendar days after first delivery of the final report, the trigger date occurs on day 60 and destruction proceeds. Any unresolved dispute is thereafter conducted on the retained technical record, which will be preserved for that purpose."

That gives you a full review cycle and a correction cycle, and it means a disagreement about a report never becomes a reason for your CAD to sit in our system.

**3. Bench exhaustion is the one operational risk left.** We accept named individuals and named alternates, prior approval for new organisations and for any expansion of scope, and same-day notification with prompt revocation. The residual problem is a bench that empties mid-programme — two machinists down, a lab technician reassigned — where prior written approval with no time limit stops the test. We are not asking for a veto-free substitution right; we are asking for a clock on the approval you have already said you will not unreasonably withhold:

> "For a new individual within an organisation already listed in Annex A and within an already-approved access scope, approval is deemed given two business days after written notice unless the design owner objects on reasonable grounds relating to confidentiality or competitive conflict. A named alternate may take over immediately within that scope. New organisations and expansions of access scope require express prior written approval."

If two business days is too tight for your conflict check, the alternative we can live with is a larger pre-cleared bench at kickoff — say four alternates per role rather than two — with express approval required for anyone outside it. Tell me which you prefer; we do not need both. What we cannot carry is an open-ended approval queue for personnel inside organisations you have already cleared.

One mechanical edit: notification "that day" should read "the same day, or the next business day where the change occurs outside business hours." Our roster is authoritative and available to you on request either way.

**4. Retained record needs a legal-hold carve-out.** Two years and then deletion is fine as the ordinary rule, and we will confirm deletion within five business days. But if a claim or an accreditation or regulatory proceeding is live or reasonably anticipated at expiry, we cannot delete the evidence, and a clause requiring us to do so is one we would be signing in breach. Narrow suspension only:

> "If, at expiry, the retained record is subject to a legal hold or is required for a pending or reasonably anticipated legal, regulatory or accreditation proceeding, the affected portion may be retained, isolated from all project and commercial use, until the matter is resolved, and must then be deleted within 30 days. The testing house will notify the design owner of the portion held, the basis, and the expected duration, and will confirm deletion on release. This does not extend retention of any other part of the record."

**The trade we want to offer.** Two things we can give you that reduce your exposure, in exchange for one allowance we need.

We can supply the machining shop with a **fixture-only neutralised extract** — mating interfaces and envelope needed to design and clamp, with unrelated internal geometry suppressed — rather than any part of the full model. And we can supply the laboratory with a setup extract rather than the assembly. That materially shrinks what leaves our control, and we will describe the extract scope in Annex A so you can see what each recipient is cleared to hold.

In exchange we need a paper allowance, because "encrypted working copies" does not describe a shop floor:

> "The machining shop may make controlled printed copies of the fixture-only extract where necessary for fabrication. Each print must be uniquely numbered, logged in and out, kept in secured storage when not in use, and cross-cut shredded on completion, with the print log included in the destruction certificate. No printed copy may leave the machining shop's premises."

Logs and shred confirmations are evidence you can audit without anyone visiting a site, which fits the verification model you have already accepted.

**On the auditor**, one addition so the mechanism is operable rather than aspirational: appointed by mutual agreement, not a competitor of either party, bound by confidentiality at least as protective as this agreement, working only on documents we produce with other customers' information redacted, one review per specific concern and no reopening of a closed concern absent new evidence of material non-compliance. Cost allocation as already agreed.

If you accept the backup eligibility fix, the day-60 long-stop, the legal-hold suspension and the print allowance, and pick either the two-day deemed approval or the enlarged bench, we can close Annex A and the destruction clause on that basis.

We accept the backup eligibility fix, the day-60 destruction trigger, the limited hold on the technical record and the controlled-print allowance. We choose the **larger pre-cleared bench**. We also accept your auditor appointment and review terms. We would record the agreement as follows.

**Personnel and Annex A.** Annex A may name up to four alternates per role at kickoff. Each may take over immediately within their approved scope. Anyone outside the named bench requires express written approval before access. We will respond to a complete request for a new individual within an approved organisation and scope within two business days, giving reasons for any objection. The testing house will maintain the current roster, make it available on request, promptly revoke access when no longer needed, and notify us of a substitution the same day or the next business day if it occurs outside business hours. The agreed written confidentiality and use restrictions apply to every named person, including alternates.

**Recipient extracts and paper copies.** Annex A will limit the machining shop to the mating interfaces and envelope needed for fabrication, with unrelated geometry removed from the delivered file. It will limit the laboratory to the extract needed for setup and testing. We accept your controlled-print wording for the machining shop. Each numbered print must be cross-cut shredded when its fabrication use ends, and in all cases by the 30-day destruction deadline. The destruction certificate must include the print log reconciling every issued print to its destruction.

**Acceptance and backups.** We accept your wording measuring non-conformities against the agreed test specification and restarting the 15-business-day review period on corrected delivery. The destruction clock starts on the earliest of written or deemed acceptance, earlier termination, or day 60 after first delivery of the final report. Day 60 triggers destruction only. Any unresolved report dispute may proceed using the permitted technical record, subject to its retention terms.

Encrypted, non-selectively purgeable sets sealed in the ordinary backup cycle before live deletion qualify for run-off. Live deletion remains due by day 30, and every qualifying set must expire by day 90, both measured from the same trigger. We accept your restoration controls and certification within five business days of actual final expiry.

**Retained record.** We accept your hold wording for the affected portion of the permitted, geometry-free technical record. At the two-year expiry, the testing house will identify the portion held, the specific basis and expected duration, and certify deletion of the balance within five business days. It will delete the held portion within 30 days after the basis for the hold ends and confirm deletion within five business days thereafter.

**Verification.** We accept a mutually appointed, non-competing auditor bound by equivalent confidentiality terms, one records-only review per specific concern, the agreed cost allocation and reopening only on new evidence of material non-compliance. The auditor may certify closure after verifying compliance or completion of corrective action. An identified evidence gap can be addressed within that same review.

Please send Annex A with the shop, laboratory, named personnel and alternates, each person’s access scope, and the extract each organisation will receive. We can then approve the populated annex in writing before first disclosure.

**Annex A — structure, scopes and extracts for your approval.** Organisations, roles, access scopes and extract boundaries are fixed below so you can approve them now. Individual names and their signed undertakings are inserted in the executed version; the annex is not effective, and no disclosure occurs, until you approve the populated version in writing.

**A1 — Testing house (prime).**
Roles: test lead, vibration test engineer (2), instrumentation technician (2), data/report analyst, document controller. Four named alternates per role.
Scope: full drawings and CAD geometry as delivered, held in the encrypted project store; access limited to preparation, execution and reporting of the agreed tests. Document controller alone holds the master set and issues extracts. No download to unmanaged devices.

**A2 — Machining shop (fixtures).**
Roles: shop supervisor, CNC programmer, two machinists, quality inspector. Four named alternates per role.
Scope: **fixture-only neutralised extract** — mating interfaces, mounting hole pattern, bolt circle, envelope and mass/CG data needed to design and clamp; unrelated internal geometry removed from the delivered file before transfer. Encrypted transfer and storage; controlled numbered prints under the agreed log-and-shred terms; prints never leave the premises. No access to the full model, to test results, or to any other customer's material.

**A3 — Accredited laboratory (vibration runs).**
Roles: lab manager, test engineer (2), technician (2), calibration custodian. Four named alternates per role.
Scope: **setup extract** — external envelope, mounting interface, mass properties, instrumentation locations and orientation, plus the test specification. No internal geometry, no design intent detail, no fixture design files. Retains the geometry-free technical record and calibration certificates for the agreed two years.

**Two additions we need in the annex itself, both mechanical.**

*Annex updates.* New individuals inside an approved organisation and scope, and new organisations, go by express written approval with your two-business-day response to a complete request. Please add that the annex is version-controlled and that the testing house issues the updated roster with each change, so the approved annex and the live roster never diverge.

*Approval timing.* We will submit the populated annex for signature. If approval is not given within five business days of a complete submission, the programme dates shift by the delay — we are not seeking deemed approval for organisations, only recognising that the schedule cannot absorb an open queue.

**One trade worth taking before you approve the extracts.** If your side generates the neutralised fixture extract and the setup extract and delivers those to us instead of the full model, we never hold your internal geometry at all. That removes the largest item from the destruction obligation, shrinks the backup run-off to two small files, and makes the shop's print log the only paper in circulation. We would then hold the full drawings only if a specific test question requires them, requested case by case.

The cost to you is drafting effort on your side and a possible delay if a test question needs geometry you have not released. The cost to us is that we cannot resolve an unexpected interface problem ourselves — we would come back to you and wait. On a fixture-driven vibration programme that risk is manageable, and we would rather carry it than hold your model. Tell me which you want:

- **Option 1:** you supply both extracts; we hold no full geometry unless separately requested and approved.
- **Option 2:** you deliver the full model to the testing house only; we generate the extracts under the Annex A boundaries and certify what was removed, and you may review the extract files before onward transfer.

Option 2 keeps the programme moving and gives you a check on the neutralisation. Option 1 gives you the smaller footprint. Either is workable for us; we lean to Option 1 if your drafting capacity allows it before kickoff.

**Consolidated certificate contents**, so there is no argument at day 30 about what "identifying the materials destroyed" means. The signed certificate will list: categories of material destroyed and the date and method for each; live deletion completion date; written destruction confirmations from the shop and the laboratory; the print log reconciling every issued print to its shredding; confirmation that design-derived fixture features were removed or destroyed and that retained tooling embodies none of your geometry; the scope of material held under the backup run-off with its expiry dates; and the scope of the retained technical record with its two-year expiry. Backup expiry is certified separately within five business days of actual final expiry.

Confirm the extract option and the scopes above and we will send the populated annex for signature. On our side nothing else is open.

We select **Option 1**. We will prepare and supply the fixture and setup extracts. We approve the proposed roles, up to four named alternates per role, and the A2 and A3 extract boundaries. Please replace the A1 scope with the following wording.

> The testing house may hold the two design-owner-issued extracts and the agreed test specification in its encrypted project store. Access is limited to the material each named person needs for their approved role. The document controller holds the master copies of the extracts and issues the fixture extract to the machining shop and the setup extract and test specification to the laboratory. If a test question requires additional geometry, the testing house must identify the question, the specific detail needed and the proposed recipients. Any additional release requires the design owner’s express written approval of the material, recipients and scope before disclosure.

We agree to version control. Each revision must identify its effective date. The testing house will issue the current roster with each change and link it to the approved annex revision. A named alternate may take over within their approved scope on the agreed notification terms. New individuals, organisations and scope expansions require express written approval. We will respond to a complete change request within two business days.

We accept the five-business-day review period for the initial populated annex. If our review exceeds that period, affected programme dates will move by the delay attributable to our review beyond the fifth business day. We will identify any missing information promptly.

We accept the consolidated certificate contents and the separate backup-expiry certification. Please send the populated annex for signature with each organisation’s legal name, each individual’s name and scope, and the signed undertakings. First disclosure may proceed once we approve that version in writing.

**A1 accepted as worded.** Option 1 is agreed: you issue both extracts, we hold no full model, and any additional geometry comes to us only on your express written approval of material, recipients and scope.

Three conforming items and one allocation point, then we populate.

**1. Conforming edits — the destruction clause still describes a model we will not hold.** As drafted it obliges us to destroy "the drawings, CAD geometry and derivative fixture files." Under Option 1 we never receive the first two. Replace the opening object of the clause and the certificate reference throughout with:

> "the design owner-issued fixture and setup extracts, any additionally released geometry, and derivative fixture files"

Same change in the retained-record exclusion and in the backup run-off description, so the run-off now covers two small extract files rather than a model. Nothing else in the agreed destruction mechanics moves: day 30 live deletion, day 90 hard expiry, day 60 long-stop trigger, restoration controls, separate expiry certification.

**2. Additional-geometry requests need a response clock, not a deemed approval.** Your A1 wording gives us the right to ask and gives you the veto, which we accept. What it does not give is a time in which we will hear the answer, and a fixture programme cannot idle on an open question. We are not asking for deemed release of geometry — the opposite of what Option 1 is for. We ask for:

> "The design owner will respond to a complete additional-geometry request within three business days, approving in whole or part, refusing with reasons, or proposing an alternative extract. Programme dates affected by a request outstanding beyond three business days move by the delay attributable to that period."

If three is too tight for your engineering check, five with the same schedule relief works for us. The relief matters more than the number.

**3. Extract accuracy — narrow allocation.** Under Option 1 the neutralisation is done on your side and we cannot verify it against the model, by design. If an issued extract is dimensionally wrong or omits an interface feature and that causes fixture scrap or a re-test, we should not carry the cost or the schedule. Proposed:

> "The design owner is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the extracts it issues for the agreed test specification. Where an extract error causes fixture rework or a repeat test, the resulting direct cost and programme delay are for the design owner's account. The testing house must notify a suspected extract error promptly and take reasonable steps to mitigate."

We are not asking you to warrant the actuator design or the test outcome — only that the file you hand us matches the part you want tested. Our own fabrication and setup errors stay ours.

**4. Populating the annex.** Legal names, individual names, per-person scope and signed undertakings cannot be produced in this exchange, and I will not send an annex with placeholder names for you to approve. Sequence we propose:

- We issue the executed-form undertakings to each named individual and countersigned equivalents to the shop and the laboratory, on terms at least as protective as the agreement.
- We deliver the populated Annex A — legal names of all three organisations, each individual and alternate against role and scope, the extract each organisation receives, and the undertakings — within five business days of your confirmation of these conforming edits.
- Your five-business-day review runs from that complete submission, with the agreed schedule relief beyond day five and prompt notice of anything missing.
- You deliver the two extracts; first disclosure follows your written approval of that annex revision. No material moves before then.

Version control, effective dates, roster issued with each change and linked to the approved revision, same-day or next-business-day substitution notice, four alternates per role, express approval outside the bench with your two-business-day response — all as you recorded them.

Confirm the three conforming edits and the extract-error allocation, or tell me where you want them narrower, and we will start the undertakings immediately. Nothing else is open on our side.

We agree to the terminology change, the three-business-day response period and the Annex A sequence. We accept responsibility for errors in the extracts we issue on the following terms.

**Destruction and retention.** Use “the design owner-issued fixture and setup extracts, any additionally released drawings or geometry, and derivative fixture files” in the destruction, certificate and backup provisions. The retained technical record must remain geometry-free, including where a dimensioned view or extract detail has been copied into another document. Drawing number, revision index and date remain permitted. The agreed deadlines, restoration controls, print reconciliation and physical-fixture destruction requirements still apply.

**Additional geometry.** We accept your proposed wording. Within three business days of a complete request, we will approve it in whole or in part, decline it with reasons, or propose an alternative extract. Affected programme dates move by the delay attributable to a request remaining unanswered beyond that period. Each release requires express written approval of the material, recipients and scope.

**Extract accuracy.** Please use this wording:

> The design owner is responsible for the dimensional accuracy of each extract it issues against the actuator configuration identified for testing and for inclusion of the features needed within the agreed extract scope to perform the agreed test specification. The design owner will correct an erroneous extract and bear reasonable, documented direct costs of fixture rework, fixture replacement or repeat testing, together with the resulting programme delay, to the extent caused by the error or omission. The testing house must promptly notify the design owner of a suspected error and take reasonable steps to mitigate cost and delay. The testing house remains responsible for fabrication or setup errors by it or its approved recipients.

Please begin the undertakings and deliver the populated Annex A with the signed undertakings within five business days of this confirmation. Our five-business-day review starts on complete submission, with the agreed schedule relief. We will deliver the two extracts only after we approve that annex revision in writing.

**Accepted.** Your extract-accuracy wording is agreed as drafted, and the destruction, certificate and backup terminology is settled. The retained record stays geometry-free including any detail copied into another document; setup descriptions in it will be textual only, with drawing number, revision index and date as the sole design identifiers. All agreed deadlines, restoration controls, print reconciliation and physical-fixture destruction stand unchanged.

Two clarifications on the accuracy clause, neither reopening it:

- Our duty is to notify a suspected error promptly and mitigate. It is not a duty to inspect or verify the extracts against the actuator — under Option 1 we have nothing to verify them against, and we will not be treated as having accepted an extract as correct by using it. If you want that stated expressly, add: "The testing house has no obligation to verify the extracts against the actuator configuration."
- "Reasonable, documented direct costs" covers fixture rework, replacement and repeat testing as listed.
